title: Onboarding Accelerator: 14-30-60 Onramp Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, practical onramp playbook designed for high-velocity customers that need measurable product value in the first 14 days, with a clear path to product-led adoption at 30 and expansion by 60 days. The playbook balances technical enablement (API keys, endpoints, sample prompts) with product adoption rituals (check-ins, success milestones, usage goals).

Executive summary:
- Goal: Deliver two measurable customer value moments in first 14 days (one technical, one product UX) and reach baseline production usage by day 60.
- Success metric examples: API calls / day, 7-day active users, median generation latency, average cost-per-response (token units), demoable feature in customer app.
- Typical customer profile for this playbook: engineering-led, PLG-adopting SaaS or AI-native startup using Redwood Hosted API or Dedicated capacity.

Assumptions / pre-reqs before kickoff:
- Account created and org admin identified
- API key provisioned and at least one environment (dev) with access
- Sample model pinned (e.g., open-model v2.1 or Redwood-verified equivalent)
- Customer has a small pilot dataset or prompt set to test with (3–10 prompts)
- Slack channel or shared space established for fast comms

14-day quick-win sprint (primary objective: two value moments)
Day 0 (Kickoff):
- 30-minute intro call: scope, decision-maker, demo target, security/PII constraints.
- Share quickstart repo and one-click Postman/CLI example configured to customer org.
- Assign owner and SLOs: latency target, cost cap, and 14-day success checklist.

Days 1–3 (technical unblock):
- Validate API key, region routing, and basic generate request. Capture initial latency.
- Run single-threaded sample with customer prompt set. Record outputs and note quality issues.
- If Dedicated/Private onboarding: confirm network rules (VPC peering/egress), KMS integration checklist started.

Days 4–8 (product integration and first demo):
- Embed generation into a small demo flow in customer app (search augmentation, help widget, or summarization).
- Instrument telemetry: tokens per request, success/failure rates, latencies, and user-facing metrics.
- Deliver first demo to stakeholders highlighting the technical and UX value moment.

Days 9–14 (iterate & lock quick wins):
- Implement one iteration: prompt tuning, model variant switch, or simple caching to meet latency/cost targets.
- Capture before/after metrics and prepare a one-page summary for the customer.
- Validate adoption signals: daily active users, repeat queries, and feature retention.

30-day adoption plan (objective: stabilize usage & expand pilot):
Weeks 3–4:
- Monthly QBR-lite with customer: review 14-day results, adoption metrics, known quality regressions.
- Suggest Redwood Optimize levers: batching settings, prefix caching, or quantized model variant if cost is a blocker.
- Run guided experiment: A/B two model configs (through Redwood Console rollouts) and measure end-user quality and cost delta.
- CS tasks: create success milestones, note blockers, provide a prioritized backlog of integration items.

By day 30 success checklist:
- Pilot flow running in staging or limited production.
- Telemetry dashboard set up in Redwood Console (token costs, route-level latency, error rates).
- At least one automated alert for quality regression (prompt set evaluation) and one cost alert.

60-day expansion plan (objective: production readiness and renewal signals):
Weeks 6–8:
- Plan for scaling: discuss Dedicated capacity vs hosted burst strategy, identify peak windows, and sizing estimate.
- Security/compliance closure: confirm audit log access, KMS/HSM keys (if Private), and contractual SSO/SAML integration.
- Hand off to Solutions Engineering for any performance-critical latency tuning (kernel selection, KV cache sizing) if needed.

By day 60 success checklist:
- Production route(s) live with measurable traffic and SLOs being met 95% of time.
- Cost/per-response within agreed threshold or mitigation plan in place.
- Renewal health signals: product is in roadmap, usage growth > 25% week-over-week, and stakeholder NPS > 7 (qualitative).

Renewal and expansion play triggers (what to watch for):
- Positive renewal signals: sustained increase in DAU/queries, teams requesting dedicated/pinned models, interest in on-prem/private deployment for compliance.
- Risk signals: falling request success rate, unexplained latency spikes, repeated quality regressions, stalled onboarding tickets older than 2 weeks.
- CS actions on signals: escalate to eng leads, open performance ticket (SE/infra), schedule executive business review, propose Dedicated Pilot.

Operational checklists (short actionable items):
- Technical checklist: API key tested, postman/CLI example runs, console dashboard set, canary route configured, replay logs accessible.
- Product checklist: demo recorded, internal champions identified, two initial end-users trained, support runbook shared.
- Compliance checklist: data retention policy agreed, PII handling confirmed, contract SLA referenced.

Risk register (common quick blockers & mitigations):
- Blocker: High early latency. Mitigation: enable prefix caching, reduce max tokens, or switch to lower-latency model variant temporarily.
- Blocker: Cost overshoot during testing. Mitigation: set token hard caps, enable batching suggestions from Redwood Optimize, or throttle non-production keys.
- Blocker: Quality mismatch to expectations. Mitigation: curate prompt set, run small evals in Console, and schedule rapid prompt tuning session with SE.

Templates & artifacts to attach for each customer:
- Quickstart repo link (pre-configured with keys and sample prompts).
- One-page 14-day summary template (metrics before/after).
- Rollout plan template for production pinning and canary.
- Renewal playbook checklist (signals + recommended next offers).

Hand-off to account management at day 60:
- Deliver final adoption report (usage, SLOs, outstanding tech debt).
- Proposed commercial next-step: Dedicated capacity proposal or multi-month commit based on projected token usage.
- Suggested exec engagement: 30-minute roadmap alignment with product/engineering.

Notes to CS team (best practices):
- Keep early demos narrow-scoped and measurable.
- Use the smallest possible prompt set for early evals to keep noise low.
- Tie each technical change to a business metric (latency -> conversion, cost -> CAC).
- Document every experiment in the shared onboarding thread and link to JIRA tickets.

Open questions / follow-ups for internal team:
- Do we have a one-click Dedicated sizing calc for quick proposals?
- Can SEs pre-bundle a prompt-tuning session for large customers as a purchasable add-on?

Appendix (example metrics to track):
- Tokens per successful session, median generation latency, 95th percentile latency, rate of retried requests, weekly active users hitting the feature, per-route cost per 1k responses.

-- End of playbook --

Document history: created by Aisha Patel and iterated with Liam Ortiz and Nora Singh.
